## Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS

Verify ran at the full commit set, and one scenario fails: **R2.S1**.

**Files written**
- `changes/add-greeting/evidence/20261028T0417Z.md` (the evidence record)
- `changes/add-greeting/evidence/20261028T0417Z-T7-report.md` (the report)

**Results** (macos-laptop; space 5c02e1a, alpha 51682dc, beta 9b0e3e6, gamma c3c3c3c at its pin)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| R1.S1 default greeting | pass |
| R1.S2 name too long | pass |
| R2.S1 start-up line | **fail** |
| alpha unit suite (4 tests) | pass |
| beta unit suite (2 tests) | pass |
| Q1 byte-compiles, both repos | pass |
| Regression suite `tests/` | no tests in it |

Wall time: 3 s.

**The failure:** `python3 -m beta` prints `beta 1.0` first and `hello, demo` second. The spec says the greeting comes first. It ran in 0.14 s, well inside the 1 s limit, so only the line order is wrong. beta's unit suites still pass, which means they don't check the order.

**Concerns**
- **Report location:** the brief asked for the report at `tasks/T7-report.md`. My role only lets me write under `evidence/`, so I filed it there.
- **Commits checked by hand:** git commands weren't allowed in this run. I confirmed the alpha and beta commits by reading their `.git` refs, not with git itself.
- **Space commit not checked:** the space checkout isn't a git repository, so 5c02e1a is the brief's value and I couldn't confirm it.
- **gamma not run:** there's no gamma checkout on this node, so it's recorded at its pin and nothing ran against it.
- **Leftover files:** Q1 left untracked `__pycache__/` folders in the alpha and beta checkouts.

## Why

Users of `beta` want a greeting on start-up, and the text belongs in `alpha`,
the shared library, so that other tools can use it too.

## Scope

In: the greeting text in `alpha`; printing it in `beta`.

Out: translations; any change to `gamma`.

## Requirements

### R1 Greeting text
`alpha` SHALL provide the greeting `hello, demo` for a caller that asks for it.

#### R1.S1 Default greeting
- GIVEN `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with no name
- THEN it gets the exact text `hello, demo` (11 characters, no trailing
  newline)

#### R1.S2 Name too long
- GIVEN a name of 65 characters
- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with that name
- THEN it gets an error naming the 64-character limit, and no greeting

### R2 beta prints the greeting
`beta` SHALL print the greeting from `alpha` as its first line of output.

#### R2.S1 Start-up line
- GIVEN `beta` built against `alpha` at the branch head
- WHEN `beta` starts with no arguments
- THEN its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of
  start (wall time)

## Quality

### Q1 Byte-compiles
The changed code SHALL byte-compile with the node's Python 3.
- check: `python3 -m compileall -q .` in each affected repo; passing is exit
  status 0

## Approaches

1. Greeting in `alpha`, printed by `beta` (picked: one source of the text).
2. Greeting in `beta` only (rejected: other tools would copy the text).

## Open calls

1. The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points.

---
# Record: changes/<id>/evidence/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>.md, one file per verify run,
# named by its UTC start. A verify shard's record is
# changes/<id>/evidence/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-<shard id>.md, one file per shard run.
# Replace every <placeholder> and drop these comments.
# a shard's record: id: ev-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>-<shard id>
id: ev-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>
change: <id>
# a shard's record only: its shard id, and the tests the record ran, by test
# name; leave both keys out of an unsharded record
shard: <shard id>
tests: [<test name>, ...]
# every repo in pod.yaml; a repo the spec does not name, at its pin
commit_set: {space: <sha7>, <repo>: <sha7>, ...}
env: <environment class>
actor: <handle>/test
# every scenario of this change, then the regression suite's results under
# qualified ids: <change>/<Rn.Sm>; a shard gives only those it ran
scenarios: {<Rn.Sm>: pass|fail|not-run, ...}
# each affected repo's unit suite; none-present when the repo has none; a
# shard gives only those it ran
unit: {<repo>: pass|fail|none-present}
# a result for every check the spec declares, or for a shard every check it
# ran; when the spec has no Quality section, write this line instead:
# quality: none-declared
quality: {<Qn>: pass|fail}
# optional: the plan's inspection checks and the builders' test suggestions;
# leave either key out when there are none
x-checks: {<In>: pass|fail}
x-suggestions: {T<n>.TS<k>: pass|fail}
# the whole run, in s
wall_time_s: <integer>
